blocks.title: 📧 THE 6 PARTS OF AN EMAIL

cells.body: Dear Mr. Smith, / Dear Hiring Manager,
I hope you are doing well. I am writing to…
Your main point, in clear paragraphs.
I look forward to your reply.

blocks.stage: ① EMAIL STRUCTURE · partes + cortesía

blocks.title: 📘 POLITE · INDIRECT LANGUAGE
blocks.intro: Cuanto más indirecto, más educado. De directo → muy educado:

items: Could you send me the report?
Would you mind sending me the report?

parts.html: Más frases: "I would appreciate it if you could…" · "Would it be possible to…?" · "Could you kindly…?"

cells.body:
Modales: Can you… → Could you… / Would you be able to…
Contracciones: I'll → I will
color (no colour) · behavior · organize · center. Fecha: April 5. Y on the weekend.

parts.h: B2 STRETCH · voz pasiva (be + past participle)
parts.body:
Enfoca la acción, no la persona (más neutral y diplomático):
"You made a mistake." → "A mistake was made." · "You didn't send it." → "It hasn't been sent yet." · "We approved your request." → "Your request has been approved."

blocks.title: ★ RUDE vs. POLITE
blocks.intro: Vas a escuchar el mismo tipo de pedido de dos formas: Mark (directo, casi grosero) y Elena (profesional y educada). Tu misión: convertir lo directo en un email cortés.
blocks.stage: ② THE STORY · dos maneras de pedir lo mismo

blocks.title: MAKE IT POLITE

items.q: You need the report from a colleague.
options: Could you please send me the report?

items.q: You want someone to review a document.
options: Would you mind reviewing this document?

items.q: You want to know if someone can attend a 3 p.m. meeting.
options: Would you be able to attend at 3 p.m.?

items.q: You want an update on a project.
options: I would appreciate an update on the project.

items.q: Which is more formal for an email?
options: I will get back to you.

speaking.prompt: Say 3 polite requests you might make at work today. Start with "Could you…" or "Would you mind…".

blocks.stage: ③ PRACTICE · elige la respuesta

blocks.title: FIX THE EMAIL
blocks.intro: Elige la mejor opción para un email profesional.

items.q: A work email should start with…
Which is the best subject line?
To sound formal, you should avoid…
Why use the passive "A mistake was made"?
options: To focus on the action, not the person (more diplomatic)

items.q: Best way to end a request politely?
options: Thank you for your help. Best regards,

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · MARK'S VOICEMAIL
blocks.desc: Mark deja un mensaje muy directo. Escúchalo — luego lo convertirás en un email educado.

questions.q: What three things does Mark want?
options: The report today, an explanation of the numbers, and the shipment fixed
The report tomorrow, a call about the numbers, and a new date
The report today, a meeting about the numbers, and a refund
Formal and polite, but a little cold
Direct and informal — not very polite
Confused and unsure about the numbers

questions.q: What is your task after listening?
options: Forward his message to the accounts team without changes
Reply to him in the same direct tone, but shorter
Rewrite his requests as a polite, professional email

transcript.html: Hey, it's Mark. Listen, I need that report today, okay? Send it over. Also, the numbers in the last part don't make sense to me. Explain them. And we have that shipment problem. It got delayed, so fix it soon. Call me back. Bye.

blocks.stage: ④ LISTENING · directo vs. educado

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · ELENA'S POLITE CALL
blocks.desc: Elena pide lo mismo, pero de forma profesional. Fíjate en las frases educadas.

options: To follow up on the report

questions.q: Which polite phrase does she use?
options: "Please send it over before the end of today."
"Whenever you have a moment, could you please send it over?"
"I would appreciate it if you could send it today."

questions.q: What does she ask about the shipment?
options: The reason for the delay and who is at fault
The price of the shipment and the refund policy
The new delivery date and possible solutions

transcript.html: Hello, this is Elena from the accounts team. I hope you're doing well. I'm calling to follow up on the report. Whenever you have a moment, could you please send it over? I would also appreciate a short explanation of the numbers in the final section. And regarding the shipment, could you let me know the new delivery date and any possible solutions? Thank you so much for your help. Have a great day!

blocks.title: ✍️ TURN MARK INTO A POLITE EMAIL
blocks.intro: Convierte el mensaje directo de Mark en un email profesional. Incluye las 6 partes y lenguaje indirecto.
checklist: Pedidos educados: "Could you please…" / "I would appreciate…"
